source.title: Confidence Dimension for Deep Learning based on Hoeffding Inequality and Relative Evaluation
source.authors: Run-Qi Wang; Lin-Lin Yang; Bao-Chang Zhang; Wentao Zhu; D. Doermann; Guo-Dong Guo

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures its proposed confidence dimension (CD) and compares it with cross-task performance changes. It does not measure the same-distribution train/test gap or the behaviors named in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's CD values and cross-task performance changes are its own results, recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure the outcomes named by V1–V8. Citations to prior work on generalization are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates confidence dimension (CD) and transfer from classification to detection, rather than any outcome specified by V1–V8. Its half-corrupted-label training measures capacity but does not pair that result with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy as V1 requires. Optimizer comparisons report CD and training error, not the held-out performance named in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose CD as a relative-generalization measure, claim a theoretical upper-bound interpretation, and report stable rankings across classification settings and agreement with selected classification-to-detection comparisons. This is their interpretation, rather than direct validation of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a CD measure based on VC-dimension and a correction term; it does not reproduce the original memorization/generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: CD ranks and values vary across dataset, class count, training-set size, and optimizer; the paper reports more stable CD rankings than VC-dimension rankings across tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: CD consistently ranks MobileNetV2, ResNet-18, PCNN and ReActNet from lowest to highest across the reported classification variants. These are proposed generalization scores, not outcomes named in V1–V8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CD gives stable relative model rankings across the tested dataset, class-count and training-size combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: ReActNet has lower CD with AdamW than Adam, and lower CD with either than SGD. No corresponding held-out optimizer comparison is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CD rankings across SGD, Adam and AdamW remain consistent across the tested ImageNet variants.

fits_no_version.finding: PCNN has lower ImageNet classification accuracy than ReActNet but higher VOC mAP and slightly lower COCO mAP; MobileNetV2/ReAct exceeds ResNet-18/ReAct on classification and VOC detection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative classification-to-detection performance comparisons agree with the proposed CD ranking for the tested binary networks.

record.problems: The paper uses CD and cross-task performance change as generalization measures rather than reporting same-distribution train/test gaps. The paper describes relative rankings and stability, with no uncertainty estimates reported for the extracted values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1–3 training errors and p/Rank values are not extracted: they are inputs or comparator measures for the CD analysis, rather than the reported CD result. Other discussion and cited prior results are omitted.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label held-out generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level held-out performance for random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epochs and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain unlinked to V1–V8. Randomization training is used to construct CD; it does not supply the held-out comparisons required by V1. The unrecorded COCO relative decline of 2.2% concerns only cross-task validation and is not missing evidence for a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Width sweep across the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the stated local-connectivity comparisons.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train/test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
